questions.question: Which of the solid has both top and base parallel to each other?

explanations.a: A frustum has two parallel circular or polygonal faces—top and base, making it the correct answer for solids with parallel top and base.

questions.question: Solid has _____ dimension. It has length, breath and _____.

explanations.c: Solids have three dimensions: length, breadth (width), and thickness (height). These three dimensions define the complete spatial extent of any solid object.

questions.question: Solid may be divided into two groups ______ and ______.

explanations.c: Solids are categorized into two main groups: Polyhedrons (solids with flat polygonal faces) and Solids of Revolution (solids formed by rotating a plane figure around an axis).

questions.question: Prism and Pyramid are the kind of

explanations.a: Polyhedrons are solids bounded by flat polygonal faces. Both prisms and pyramids have flat faces and are therefore classified as polyhedrons.

questions.question: What is the characteristic feature of a regular polyhedron?

explanations.b: A regular polyhedron has all faces equal in size and shape, with identical angles and edge lengths, creating perfect geometric symmetry.
An icosahedron is a regular polyhedron with exactly 20 equilateral triangular faces, 12 vertices, and 30 edges.

questions.question: Which of these is a solid of revolution?

explanations.d: A cone is a solid of revolution formed by rotating a right-angled triangle around one of its perpendicular sides as the axis of rotation.

questions.question: What is the axis of a right pyramid?

explanations.a: In a right pyramid, the axis runs vertically from the center of the base to the apex and is perpendicular to the base plane.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of studying solids and their projections in engineering?

answers.b: Foundation for designing and visualizing structures

explanations.b: Understanding solid projections provides engineers with the foundation for 3D visualization, design development, and accurate representation of structures and components.

questions.question: What does the term "frustum" refer to in the context of solids?

answers.a: The top portion of a cone or pyramid removed by a parallel plane
answers.b: A solid cut by a plane inclined to its base
answers.d: A cube with equal square faces

explanations.a: A frustum is the remaining portion of a cone or pyramid after the top part has been removed by a cutting plane parallel to the base.

questions.question: Dodecahedron has twelve and all equal ________________ as faces.

explanations.a: A dodecahedron is a regular polyhedron consisting of twelve identical regular pentagonal faces, with each vertex joining three pentagons.

questions.question: A right circular cone is a solid generated by the revolution of a ______________ about one of its perpendicular sides which is fixed.

explanations.b: A right circular cone is formed by rotating a right-angled triangle about one of its perpendicular sides (usually the height) as the axis of rotation.

questions.question: The top of the pyramid is known as

explanations.b: The apex is the highest point of a pyramid where all the triangular faces meet at a single vertex, forming the tip of the structure.

questions.question: Which of the following solids is generated by revolving a rectangle around one of its sides?

explanations.a: A cylinder is formed by revolving a rectangle around one of its sides (usually the longer side) as the axis of rotation, creating circular cross-sections.

questions.question: In a truncated solid, what kind of cut is made?

explanations.b: A truncated solid is formed by making an inclined cut (at an angle) to the base of the solid, creating an irregular cross-section different from the original shape.
